newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN MULLS INTL BOND TO COVER DEFICIT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN MULLS INTL BOND TO COVER DEFICIT.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry on Friday said it was considering issuing an unspecified tranche of international bonds later this year to help cover its 1997 planned budget deficit.
"We have this opportunity (to issue an international bond) and we are thinking about it," Marian Horvath, head of the ministry's State Assets and Liabilities Department, told Reuters.
But he added that "serious consideration" of the move was not expected earlier than in the second half of the year.
"Of course, we will act according to the situatin on the interbank market, but I think that the issuance is not likely in coming months," he said.
Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik on Friday told the daily Pravda that the government may turn to foreign bonds to avoid the negative influence of high local interest rates on re-financing the deficit.
The goverment plans to run a budget deficit of 36.9 billion crowns this year, up from a shortfall of 25 billion in 1996.
Slovak interbank money rates on Friday ranged between 16 and 17 percent for terms from one week to six months.
The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has called for a more cautious approach in governemnt investment projects, warning that some larger programmes may endanger currency stability.

The government's development programmes for next year include 14 billion crowns for motorway construction and multi-billion crown government guarantees for modernisation of the state-run railway system and hydro-construction projects.
The cabinet is expected to issue some 70 billion crowns in state securities on the domestic market this year to cover 1996 and 1997 deficits.
The central bank has also warned that the ecomony is showing the first signs of overheating and that it would stick to a strict monetary policy to keep inflation under control.
CPI rose 1.1 percent month-on-month in January, putting prices 5.8 percent higher year-on-year.
